record.paper_title: Some open problems of graph theory.
record.original_question: Determine all 2-connected r-regular graphs for which there is a Hamiltonian circuit or a cycle of length 2r + 4.

evidence.quote: Problem 8. (H.-J. Voss) On determining all 2-connected r-regular graphs for which the length of a Hamiltonian circuit or a cycle is equal to \(2r+4.\)

artifact.self_contained_problem: For an integer $r \geq 2$, characterize all finite simple 2-connected $r$-regular graphs $G$ with the following property: $G$ contains either a Hamiltonian cycle or a cycle of length exactly $2r+4$. Equivalently, determine the complete list (up to isomorphism) of 2-connected $r$-regular graphs whose circumference equals $2r+4$, together with those that are Hamiltonian.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface a published classification answering this question. Related work by Voss and others on circumference and longest cycles in 2-connected graphs exists, but no source verifying a complete characterization of 2-connected r-regular graphs whose longest cycle has length 2r+4 (or is Hamiltonian) was found.

status_evidence.title: Longest Cycles in 2-Connected Graphs with Prescribed Maximum Degree
status_evidence.snippet: Bounds on circumference of 2-connected graphs in terms of degree.
status_evidence.claim: Related circumference bounds exist but do not give the requested characterization.

status_evidence.title: Proof of a conjecture of Voss on bridges of longest cycles
status_evidence.snippet: Voss's conjecture concerns bridges of longest cycles, distinct from this problem.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work on Voss-related conjectures does not address this specific characterization.
